<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />{{GHGmargin-letter|117|w}}
2. The modification of the original meaning becomes especially evident when even reflexive conjugations (''Niphʿal, Hithpaʿēl'', &c.) take an accusative (cf. § 57, note 2); e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נִבָּא|translate=to prophesy}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָסַב}} (prop. ''to put oneself round'') ''to surround'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַם|translate=to fight}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=3}} (where, however, the {{GHGterm|Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּלְחֲמ֫וּנִי}} should be read; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=1}}); also {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגַּלַּח|translate=to shave}} (something) ''for oneself'', Num 6:19; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַחֵל|translate=to take}} some one ''for oneself as a possession'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַכֵּל|translate=to make}} some one ''an object of craft'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַצֵּל|translate=to strip}} a thing ''off oneself'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעַבֵּר|translate=to bring on oneself the anger}} of any one, ''to anger'' him; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְבּוֹנֵן|translate=to consider}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפָּרֵק|translate=to break}} something ''off from oneself'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=3}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=9}} after {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַתְּנוּ|translate=make ye marriages}}, read {{GHGheb|text=אִתָּ֫נוּ}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=אֹתָ֫נוּ}}. Cf. {{GHGpar|54|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|x}}
3. So also it is only owing to a modification of the original meaning of a verb (except where the expression is incorrect, and perhaps derived from the popular language), when sometimes the remoter object (otherwise introduced by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}) is directly subordinated in the form of an accusative suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲצוֹם צַמְתֻּ֫נִי אָ֫נִי|translate=did ye fast at all unto me, even to me?}} as though to say, have ye ''be-fasted'' me? have ye reached me with your fasting? Still more strange is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֵלַ֫נִי כְאָב|translate=he}} (the orphan) ''grew up to me as to a father''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=3}}, and in Aramaic {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=6}}; but {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ הַנֶּ֫גְב נְתַתָּ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=19}} is to be regarded as a double accusative after a verb of ''giving'', see ff. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=25}} read {{GHGheb|text=וּפִלְלוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וּפִלְלוֹ}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=21}}, instead of the Niphʿal, read {{GHGheb|text=תִּנְשֵׁ֫נִי}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=29|verse=3}} either {{GHGheb|text=עֲשִׂיתִיו}} is to be read with Olshausen or {{GHGheb|text=עֲשִׂיתִים}} (and previously {{GHGheb|text=יְאֹרָי}}) with Smend; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶדַּדֶּה}} or {{GHGheb|text=אֲדַדֵּם}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=23}} (where König takes {{GHGheb|text=יְהָֽבְךָ}} as ''he has given it to thee'') we must certainly assume a substantive {{GHGheb|text=יְהָב}} (= ''fate''?).

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|y}}
4. Whole classes of verbs, which, according to ''v'' above, are regarded as ''transitive'', either on account of their original meaning or (for the sake of analogy) by a modification of that meaning, are—

(''a'') Verba ''induendi'' and ''exuendi'', as {{GHGheb|text=לָבַשׁ|translate=to put on}}, {{GHGheb|text=פָּשַׁט|translate=to put off}} a garment, {{GHGheb|text=עָדָה|translate=to put on}} ornaments, ''to adorn oneself with'' (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מְשֻׁבָּצִים זָהָב|translate=enclosed in gold}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=20}}). Also in poetic expressions such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=לָֽבְשׁוּ כָּרִים הַצֹּאן|translate=the pastures are clothed with flocks}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=29}}; 104:2 ({{GHGheb|text=עָטָה}}); 65:14b ({{GHGheb|text=עָטַף}}), &c.<ref>From the idea of ''covering oneself with'' something, we might also, if necessary, explain {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=יִרְחֲצוּ מַיִם|translate=they shall wash themselves with water}}; but the reading is simply to be emended to the ordinary {{GHGheb|text=בַּמַּיִם}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|z}}
(''b'') Verba ''copiae'' and ''inopiae'' (also called verba ''abundandi'' and ''deficiendi''), as {{GHGheb|text=מָלֵא}}, ''to be full of'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=17}}; here, and also frequently elsewhere, construed with {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}, and hence evidently with an accusative; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=13}}; with a personal object, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=9|translate=my lust shall be satisfied upon them}}; with an accusative ''preceding'' the verb for the sake of emphasis, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}} ''your hands'' {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִים מָלֵ֫אוּ|translate=are full of blood}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=2}}; so also the ''Niph.'' {{GHGheb|text=נִמְלָא|translate=to fill oneself with}} something, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=7}} (where the object is connected by {{GHGheb|text=את}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=7}} f., 6:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִזְרַע|translate=to be fructified with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁרַץ|translate=to swarm with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=20}}, 21 {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=(שָׂבֵעַ) שָׂבַע|translate=to be full of}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּבַר|translate=to become strong, to wax mighty in}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=פָּרַץ|translate=to overflow with}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=10}} (with the object preceding); {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}} prop. ''to descend'', poetically also ''to pour down, to overflow with'' something (cf. in Greek προρέειν ὕδωρ, δάκρυα στάζειν), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=48}} {{GHGheb|text=פַּלְגֵי מַ֫יִם תֵּרַד עֵינִי|translate=mine eye runneth }}<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
